questions.text: A hospital's Emergency Department turns away a patient who presents with chest pain because the patient has no insurance. Under which federal law is this a violation?
questions.explanation: EMTALA requires all hospitals with emergency departments to provide a Medical Screening Examination and stabilize any patient presenting with an emergency medical condition, regardless of ability to pay. Turning away the patient constitutes a direct EMTALA violation and risks loss of all Medicare and Medicaid funding.

questions.text: A ransomware attack exposes 600 patient records at a regional hospital. Which combination of federal laws is triggered?

options.b: HIPAA, HITECH, and the 21st Century Cures Act

questions.explanation: A breach of PHI triggers HIPAA (Privacy Rule violation), HITECH (mandatory 60-day breach notification and business associate liability), and if the attack disables the EHR, the 21st Century Cures Act provisions on information blocking may apply. This mirrors the cross-law scenario presented in the Statutory Matrix.

questions.text: A quality director submits adverse event data to a federally listed Patient Safety Organization. Which federal law protects this data from being used in litigation?

options.b: Patient Safety and Quality Improvement Act (PSQIA)

questions.explanation: PSQIA established Patient Safety Work Product (PSWP) protection for data submitted to a PSO. This protection exists specifically to encourage honest error reporting without fear of legal discovery, supporting a Just Culture environment.

questions.text: A hospital is penalized by CMS for having an above-average 30-day readmission rate for heart failure patients. Which ACA provision triggers this financial penalty?
questions.explanation: The ACA established the HRRP, which imposes financial penalties on hospitals with excess readmissions for specified conditions including heart failure, pneumonia, and hip/knee replacement. This represents the ACA's shift from volume-based to value-based care accountability.

questions.text: An EHR vendor deliberately prevents a patient from accessing their own electronic health information through a proprietary system lock. Under which federal law is this a violation?
questions.explanation: The 21st Century Cures Act explicitly prohibits "information blocking" — the practice of deliberately impeding patient or provider access to health data. Violations carry civil monetary penalties enforced by the OIG. This is distinct from HIPAA, which governs privacy and security of PHI rather than access obstruction.
